Mole Poblano

Served at: Dia de los Muertos

Serves 8-10Prep 1 hour 30 minCook 2 hours 30 min

Mole Poblano is a rich, complex, and deeply symbolic sauce, often considered Mexico's national dish. For Dia de los Muertos, it is a quintessential offering on altars (ofrendas) and a centerpiece of the celebratory feast, honoring ancestors with its profound flavors and the labor of love involved in its preparation. Its intricate blend of chiles, spices, nuts, and chocolate represents the fusion of indigenous and European cultures.

Ingredients

  • 6 dried Ancho chiles (about 60 g)
  • 4 dried Mulato chiles (about 40 g)
  • 4 dried Pasilla chiles (about 40 g)
  • 2 dried Chipotle chiles (about 20 g, optional, for heat)
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) lard or vegetable oil, plus more for frying
  • 1/2 cup (70 g) raw almonds
  • 1/4 cup (35 g) raw peanuts
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) raisins
  • 1 small corn tortilla, torn
  • 1 slice (about 1 oz/28 g) stale bread (like bolillo or French bread), torn
  • 1/2 ripe plantain, sliced (about 3 oz/85 g)
  • 1 medium white onion, roughly chopped (about 1 cup/160 g)
  • 4 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 2 medium tomatoes, roughly chopped (about 1 cup/180 g)
  • 2 tomatillos, husked and roughly chopped (about 4 oz/110 g)
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) ground cumin
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) ground coriander
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 ml) ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 ml) ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 ml) black pepper
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 ml) dried oregano
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 ml) dried thyme
  • 1/2 tablet (about 1.5 oz/42 g) Mexican chocolate (like Ibarra or Abuelita), roughly chopped
  • 6-8 cups (1.4-1.9 L) chicken broth, warm
  • 1-2 tablespoons (15-30 ml) granulated sugar, or to taste
  • 1-2 teaspoons (5-10 ml) salt, or to taste
  • Cooked chicken pieces (e.g., thighs, drumsticks) for serving

Method

  1. Carefully remove stems and seeds from all dried chiles. Heat a dry comal or skillet over medium heat and toast the chiles for 30-60 seconds per side until fragrant but not burnt. Place toasted chiles in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft.
  2. While chiles rehydrate, heat 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of lard or oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Fry the almonds, peanuts, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, raisins, tortilla, bread, and plantain in separate batches until golden brown and fragrant. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
  3. In the same pot, add a little more oil if needed. Fry the chopped onion and garlic until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the chopped tomatoes and tomatillos and cook for another 5-7 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
  4. Drain the rehydrated chiles, reserving the soaking liquid. In a blender, combine the drained chiles, all the fried nuts, seeds, fruits, tortilla, bread, plantain, fried onion, garlic, tomatoes, and tomatillos. Add the ground cumin, coriander, cloves, cinnamon, black pepper, oregano, and thyme.
  5. Add 1-2 cups (240-480 ml) of the reserved chile soaking liquid or chicken broth to the blender. Blend until very smooth. This may require blending in batches and adding more liquid as needed to achieve a thick, pourable paste. For an extra smooth mole, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve.
  6. Heat 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of fresh lard or oil in the same large pot over medium-low heat. Carefully pour the mole paste into the hot fat. Cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for at least 30-45 minutes. This step is crucial for developing the mole's deep flavor and color; the paste will darken and thicken, and the fat will separate slightly.
  7. Gradually add the warm chicken broth, about 1 cup (240 ml) at a time, stirring continuously to incorporate it smoothly into the paste. Bring the mole to a gentle simmer after each addition. Continue adding broth until the mole reaches your desired consistency (it should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon).
  8. Stir in the chopped Mexican chocolate, sugar, and salt. Continue to simmer for at least 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the chocolate to fully dissolve. Taste and adjust seasoning with more sugar or salt as needed.
  9. Serve the Mole Poblano hot over cooked chicken pieces. Garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

Tips

  • For a deeper flavor, roast the chicken pieces in the oven before adding them to the mole to simmer for the last 15-20 minutes, allowing them to absorb the sauce.
  • Mole Poblano can be made ahead of time. Its flavors deepen overnight, making it an excellent dish for holiday preparations. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
  • If you prefer a vegetarian version, use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth and serve with roasted vegetables or plant-based protein.
